verdicts.title: Lower Bounds for Tropical Circuits and Dynamic Programs
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: Tropical circuits are circuits with Min and Plus, or Max and Plus operations as gates. Their importance stems from their intimate relation to dynamic programming algorithms. The power of tropical circuits lies somewhere between that of monotone boolean circuits and monotone arithmetic circuits. In this paper we present some lower bounds arguments for tropical circuits, and hence, for dynamic programs.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns lower bounds for tropical (Min/Plus, Max/Plus) circuits and dynamic programming, with no mention of local systems, complement graphs, or rank bounds for Boolean circuit satisfiability. It shares only the generic 'circuits' vocabulary with the conjecture.

verdicts.title: A Novel Application of Boolean Functions with High Algebraic Immunity in Minimal Codes
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: Boolean functions with high algebraic immunity are important cryptographic primitives in some stream ciphers. verdicts.title: Arithmetic Circuits with Locally Low Algebraic Rank
